Consult Summary:
- Patient with known eczema presenting with a multi-day, worsening widespread itchy, dry, sore rash involving chest, hands, arms, and antecubital fossae; prescribed topical steroid (betnovate), oral antihistamine (fexofenadine), and advised continuation of emollients.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Widespread itchy, dry, sore skin for the past few days.
  - Most affected areas: chest, hands, arms, especially inside of the elbows (antecubital fossae).
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began "over the past few days."
  - Patient reports recent worsening over the last few days.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Scratching due to itchiness; patient reports scratching but no obvious scratch marks.
  - Currently uses emollients (Diprobase) and shower product ("Dermol"/"dermal"); no change noted with continued use.
  - Patient has previously used OTC hydrocortisone; patient reports steroid use but it has not helped.
  - Patient previously tried an OTC antihistamine (reported as ineffective).
- Associated symptoms/system review:
  - No weeping or watery discharge from lesions.
  - Some skin cracking reported in affected areas.
  - No reported thickened or hyperpigmented skin.
  - No fever, no joint pains.
  - Asthma history; breathing currently "OK" and uses blue inhaler PRN for flares.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No current systemic symptoms (fever, joint pain).
  - No active infection signs reported.
  - No documented medication allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Eczema (history of recurrent eczema; current flare).
- Asthma (uses blue reliever inhaler PRN; not on regular inhaled therapy per history).

Medications:
- Diprobase (emollient) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- "Dermol"/"dermal" shower product — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- OTC hydrocortisone (topical) — dose/route/frequency not documented; patient reports prior use without improvement.
- Prior OTC antihistamine (patient-reported; likely cetirizine per clinician) — dose/route/frequency not documented; reportedly ineffective.
- Salbutamol (blue inhaler) PRN — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- New prescriptions from this visit:
  - Fexofenadine — dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript.
  - Betnovate (topical steroid, betamethasone) — topical application instructed twice daily for next couple of weeks; apply a fingertip amount sufficient to cover affected areas (specific potency/duration as stated by clinician).
Allergies:
- No known medication allergies (patient-reported).

Social History:
- Lives in London (address partially provided).
- Smoking status: not documented.
- Alcohol use: not documented.
- Substance use: not documented.
- Occupation/financial or other lifestyle factors: not documented.

Family History:
- Mother: migraine and hypothyroidism (patient-reported).

Physical Examination:
- No formal physical examination findings documented in the transcript.

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results documented or ordered in the transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Eczema exacerbation (widespread, pruritic, dry, sore; worst in antecubital fossae)
  - Assessment: Clinical diagnosis of an extensive eczema flare based on history.
  - Plan:
    - Prescribe topical potent steroid (Betnovate; betamethasone) topical — apply a fingertip amount to affected areas twice daily for the next couple of weeks (as instructed).
    - Continue regular emollients: Diprobase and the shower product ("Dermol"/"dermal").
    - Prescribe oral antihistamine fexofenadine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Advise to return or contact service if no improvement after two weeks or if symptoms worsen or adverse reactions occur.
    - Prescription sent to Boots pharmacy for collection.
- Issue 2: Pruritus (symptom related to eczema)
  - Assessment: Significant itch contributing to discomfort.
  - Plan:
    - Fexofenadine prescribed (see above).
    - Continue emollients and topical steroid as above.
- Issue 3: Asthma (stable per history)
  - Assessment: Intermittent asthma managed with PRN inhaler; no current acute respiratory symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Continue blue inhaler as needed for flares (no changes prescribed).

General Plan items:
- Patient advised on topical steroid application technique (small fingertip amount covers palms/back of hands; use minimal effective amount).
- Continue current emollient regimen alongside prescribed treatments.
- Follow-up if no improvement within two weeks or earlier if worsening/adverse effects.
- Pharmacy prescription arranged (Boots).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs recorded.
  - No documented focused physical examination of skin (inspection/extent/severity).
  - No documented steroid potency/duration beyond "couple of weeks" for betnovate (potency inferred by drug name only as given).
  - No specific doses, routes, or frequencies documented for fexofenadine or other prior OTC medications.
  - No documented smoking/alcohol/substance use or occupation.
  - No medication reconciliation with exact current asthma regimen.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Family history: patient stated mother has hypothyroidism; clinician at one point stated "she has hyperthyroidism" (conflict noted between patient-reported hypothyroidism and clinician statement).
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall adequate quality; occasional short inaudible segments and some clinician/patient misstatements, but clinical history and plan are clearly documented.
